decisions.claim: splitAvailableFor('linux','windows') returns true, contradicting acceptance check 26
decisions.reason: The contradiction is real and the SPEC was the wrong half. Making it false would put the Windows paths out of reach of CI on Linux, which is exactly how the port lock shipped broken to macOS. Verified the safety property still holds: under shape 'windows' on Linux, boundaryIsReal() calls windowsBoundaryIsReal, which needs icacls, which Linux does not have, so it returns false. Check 26 rewritten to assert that directly instead of by proxy, and the win32 half kept as it was.

decisions.claim: windowsStateRoot() adopts any inheritance-free ACL with no broad-group allow, even one an unrelated local user owns
decisions.reason: Confirmed and worse than stated: a second local account could grant exactly itself and you, pass the check, and read every credential the daemon then stored. windowsAclIsRestricted now requires the directory be private to US (windowsAclIsPrivate with our own SID), not merely free of broad groups.

decisions.claim: the ACL report has only access entries, so boundaryIsReal can return true while inheritance is enabled
decisions.reason: Confirmed. Per-entry IsInherited is the consequence, AreAccessRulesProtected is the flag, and a directory with inheritance on but a parent that has no inheritable ACEs yet shows neither. The report now carries PROTECTED and both ACL checks require it. The verifier checks it separately.

decisions.claim: WUNDERVAULT_PRINCIPAL_ID lets the environment override the account SID, so principalId() is not an identity
decisions.reason: Confirmed, and the override turned out to be used by nothing -- no test set it. Removed outright. It keyed the lock port and the derived store key, which is not something an environment variable should be able to answer.

decisions.claim: withHello decodes each TCP chunk independently and re-encodes the remainder, corrupting multi-byte characters
decisions.reason: Confirmed, and embarrassing: agent.ts documents this exact bug at length, and the new wrapper sitting in front of that handler reintroduced it twice -- once decoding per chunk, once re-encoding the remainder with Buffer.from(rest,'utf8'). Both sides now accumulate Buffers, decode only one complete line, and hand the remainder on as bytes.

decisions.claim: blind spot: the ACL model checks allow entries but not the directory's OWNER
decisions.reason: Promoted to a real bug. On Windows an owner holds READ_CONTROL and WRITE_DAC implicitly, so a state directory owned by the agents' account is one they can unlock at will -- the DACL excludes them only until they decide otherwise. The report now carries OWNER, windowsAclIsPrivate requires it be Administrators, SYSTEM or the service account, the installer sets it explicitly with icacls /setowner, and the verifier checks it.

decisions.claim: blind spot: withHello has no handshake deadline, so a client that never sends a newline holds a socket for ever
decisions.reason: Confirmed. Every timeout the real handler sets is armed inside onConnection, so nothing bounded the connection before hand-off -- the exact resource-hold shape agent.ts is careful about, with a new wrapper in front of all of it. A 10s unref'd deadline now destroys a socket that has not handed over.

decisions.claim: blind spot: unverified whether anything stops two brokers publishing the same discovery file
decisions.reason: Nothing did, and it is not hypothetical -- it happened during this phase's testing when a mistyped flag started a second broker as the wrong user and the discovery files followed it. Two fixes: an unrecognised option now exits 2 instead of starting a daemon (a bug on every platform since phase 4), and on a port-addressed platform the daemon probes the recorded port before publishing and refuses if something answers. Documented as a check, not a lock: two daemons starting in the same millisecond could still both find nothing.
